newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PALFFY SCORES TWICE TO LEAD ISLANDERS PAST FLYERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PALFFY SCORES TWICE TO LEAD ISLANDERS PAST FLYERS.

text.p: Hours after being named NHL Player of the Week for his play last week, Zigmund Palffy scored twice to lift the New York Islanders to a 4-3 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers on Monday.
Palffy picked up his eighth and ninth goals, including the game winner at 11:20 of the third period, as the Islanders erased a 3-2 deficit to win consecutive games for the first time this season.

Palffy, who scored at 11:09 of the first period to tie the game 1-1, snapped a 3-3 tie when he took a pass from Derek King and rifled a wrist shot between the pads of Flyers goaltender Ron Hextall. King also set up Palffy's first goal.

"I feel great. I'm working hard in practice and it's coming together," said Palffy, who has six goals in his last three games. "We are happy to get wins right now. We are feeling very confident and it's more fun to be winning."

Islander tough guy Mick Vukota's first goal in more than a year knotted the score 3-3 with 3:10 left in the second. The win was the first this season for New York goalie Tommy Salo, who stopped 22 shots.
Two of the Islanders' three wins have come at the expense of Philadelphia.
"We self-destructed out there tonight," said Flyers coach Terry Murray. "Just a completely unacceptable effort."
In Detroit, Doug Brown had two goals and two assists for a career-high four points to spark the Red Wings to a 5-1 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Brown opened the scoring just under three minutes into the game and Sergei Fedorov made it 2-0 21 seconds later, putting home a rebound of a Brown shot.
Brown also assisted on Vyacheslav Kozlov's sixth goal of the season to open a 4-1 lead and capped the scoring with a goal at 16:51 of the second period.
Geoff Sanderson scored the lone goal for Hartford, which is winless in its last five games.
Chris Osgood made 27 saves for Detroit, while Hartford's Sean Burke faced 38 shots and turned aside 33.

In New York, Alexander Selivanov's goal with 69 seconds left put Tampa Bay ahead for the first time as the Lightning scored four unanswered goals to beat the Rangers 5-3 and snap a five-game winless streak.
Selivanov broke a 3-3 tie after Tampa Bay's John Cullen and New York's Bill Berg crashed into Rangers goaltender Mike Richter, taking him out of the play.
The Rangers, with an extra attacker, got off several shots during the final minute but were repeatedly frustrated by Tampa Bay's Corey Schwab, who finished with 35 saves.

Dino Ciccarelli iced the win with an empty net goal with two seconds left. It was his second goal of the game and moved him ahead of Hall of Famer Guy Lafleur into 10th place on the all-time goal scoring list with 561.
Luc Robitaille scored twice for the Rangers, who led 3-1 midway through the second period. Wayne Gretzky assisted on the first goal, extending his scoring streak to 15 games.
In Boston, Mattias Timander scored his first NHL goal with 64 seconds left in regulation to lift the Bruins into a 4-4 tie with the Los Angeles Kings.

Timander's one-timer from the left point hit Stephane Fiset's blocker, flipped over the goaltender's head and skipped over the goal line as defenceman Rob Blake made a vain attempt to keep the puck out of the net.
The goal came 3:31 after the Kings had grabbed a 4-3 lead on Kai Nurminen's goal.
The Bruins outshot Los Angeles 7-1 in overtime but could not get the puck past Fiset, who finished with 33 saves.
Jozef Stumpel scored twice and Rick Tocchet had three assists for Boston. Ray Ferraro, Vladimir Tsyplakov and Blake also scored for Los Angeles.
